pr_title: rpc: reduce certificate-related allocations during authentication
pr_body:
#### rpc: add authenication benchmark

Release note: None

#### rpc: reduce certificate-related allocations during authentication

This commit avoids certificate-related allocations in the happy path of
authenticating network requests.

Release note: None

#### security: inline getCertificatePrincipals

The `getCertificatePrincipals` function has been inlined into its one
callsite to avoid allocating a slice of the results.

Fixes #133317

Release note: None

issue_context.title: rpc,security: optimize kvAuth for performance (0.5% cpu)
issue_context.body: on the sysbench oltp_read_write reference workload, authenticating incoming RPCs accounted for ~0.5% of sampled CPU time. This seems to be driven primarily by allocations such as these. We should optimize this code. As an aside: it's possible that some of the overhead of repeat authorization could be removed (within a tenant) by using long-lived streaming RPCs instead. IIRC Internally, unary RPCs are just special-cased streaming RPCs, anyway. ``` github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/security.getCertificatePrincipals pkg/security/auth.go Total: 20ms 320ms (flat, cum) 0.15% 188 . . } 189 . . return mappedName 190 . . } 191 . . 192 . . func getCertificatePrincipals(cert *x509.Certificate) []string { 193 . 210ms results := make([]string, 0, 1+len(cert.DNSNames)) 194 10ms 60ms results = append(results, transformPrincipal(cert.Subject.CommonName)) 195 . . for _, name := range cert.DNSNames { 196 10ms 50ms results = append(results, transformPrincipal(name)) 197 . . } 198 . . return results 199 . . } 200 . . 201 . . // GetCertificateUserScope extracts the certificate scopes from a client ``` Jira issue: CRDB-43616
comments: @nvanbenschoten this doesn't show up in the microbenchmark (I didn't check the version you merged but the cpu.pb.gz [here](https://cockroachlabs.slack.com/archives/C4X2J0RH6/p1730489526419859?thread_ts=1730489282.192089&cid=C4X2J0RH6), assuming they're similar). Maybe that's ok, just wanted to point it out. Maybe it's relatively easy to change the benchmark to using a secure cluster (if that is why it's not in the profile).

With the local RPC fast path disabled in the microbenchmark, I do see this code being hit, but it accounts for much less of the CPU profile. Only about .01%. Maybe it is using a cert with fewer principals.

review_comments: Which of the benchmarks reflects the case we're seeing in the sysbench reference workload? Could you add inline comments about when we expect to hit which?
this escapes to the heap (?) but could be sync.Pooled in principle.
